daily.title: US judge extends media outlets' White House access
daily.summary: A federal judge extended the order that blocks the Trump administration from banning three media outlets from the White House. The outlets have reasonable grounds to think they'll win the case, the judge said.

daily.title: Houthis launch fresh wave of missiles across Saudi Arabia
daily.summary: Both the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition carried out strikes targeting energy infrastructure. Four people were injured as a result of debris of intercepted missiles in Riyadh. DW has the latest.

daily.title: Cornell suspends frat parties after gang rape case
daily.summary: Cornell said no parties will be held at frat houses until the end of the academic year. The university is trying to mend its reputation following its handling of a gang rape case in 2024.

daily.title: OpenAI says employee caught planting listening device
daily.summary: A Saudi national employed by the artificial intelligence lab has been arrested after a listening device was planted in a company conference room.

daily.title: Vatican confirms Pope Leo underwent surgery for lung cancer
daily.summary: The pope has had part of his lung removed and is recovering after surgery. Leo has been unusually candid for a pontiff about his health issues, disclosing the surgery to thousands of people in St. Peter's Square.

daily.title: Tupac Shakur murder trial: Former gang leader Duane Davis sentenced to 40 years
daily.summary: Former Los Angeles gang leader Duane "Keffe D" Davis was found guilty of ordering the killing of hip-hop icon Tupac Shakur

daily.title: Germany news: Left-leaning Berlin coalition talks break down
daily.summary: The SPD and Greens in Berlin have halted exploratory coalition talks with the Left Party amid a dispute over Israel policy and antisemitism. DW has more.

daily.title: Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
daily.summary: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

daily.title: Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
daily.summary: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president’s decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.

daily.title: Iran seeking 'harder targets' for attacks abroad, UK warns
daily.summary: The warning from the head of the UK's domestic security agency comes after PM Burnham said an attempted plot at an air force base hosting US bombers was "almost certainly" coordinated in Tehran.

daily.title: Saudi Arabia's military struggle against Houthi attacks
daily.summary: Houthi attacks on airports and energy facilities are putting Saudi Arabia under pressure. Could a Saudi-led international military offensive succeed against the Iran-aligned Houthi militia in Yemen?

daily.title: How will emergency rule in Pakistan's northwest affect Afghan ties?
daily.summary: Pakistan's decision to suspend Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's provincial government could further strain already tense relations between Islamabad and Kabul.

daily.title: Kimberly Guilfoye: US ambassador to Greece resigns amid misconduct allegations
daily.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle has resigned as US ambassador to Greece. President Trump previously said he was unhappy with her amid reports of a bribery scandal and ethics violations.

daily.title: Hungary's parliament votes to reverse anti-LGBTQ legislation from Orban era
daily.summary: Hungary's parliament passed a bill amending the 2021 "child protection law." The move is considered the first significant reversal of Orban's curbs targeting the LGBTQ+ community.

daily.title: DR Congo: Kabila’s move towards M23 raises questions over peace
daily.summary: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political-military front that brings together the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 coalition. Analysts say it could reshape opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi.

daily.title: India: Can 'cockroaches' threaten Modi's political grip?
daily.summary: Thousands detained, leaders arrested on arrival, and a capital under lockdown: The youth-led protests against the election chief have the attention of the Indian government. But experts say toppling it is another matter.

daily.title: Nuremberg airport briefly closed after in-flight emergency
daily.summary: Police are investigating a suspected in-flight emergency on a Corfu flight. After the airport reopened, the airline said they believed the emergency code was a result of a technical malfunction.

daily.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
daily.summary: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

daily.title: Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
daily.summary: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

daily.title: Houthis and Saudis strike each other in latest escalation
daily.summary: Fighting has continued between Iran-backed rebels and Saudi Arabia, adversely impacting the kingdom's economy and security. Still, Saudi officials have stopped warning of Houthi attacks in an effort to calm fears.

daily.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
daily.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

daily.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
daily.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

daily.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
daily.summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

daily.title: What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
daily.summary: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

weekly.title: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.

weekly.title: Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
weekly.summary: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."

weekly.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
weekly.summary: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

weekly.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
weekly.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

weekly.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
weekly.summary: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

weekly.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
weekly.summary: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

weekly.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
weekly.summary: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

weekly.title: Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
weekly.summary: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

weekly.title: German 'lawfare': When lawsuits become a political weapon
weekly.summary: The Left Party is suing two government ministers for accusing them of antisemitism, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz has been sued several times by various parties. Is German politics descending into "lawfare?"

weekly.title: Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
weekly.summary: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

weekly.title: Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
weekly.summary: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

weekly.title: Germany's population is shrinking but not everywhere
weekly.summary: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.

weekly.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
weekly.summary: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

weekly.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
weekly.summary: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.

weekly.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
weekly.summary: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

weekly.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
weekly.summary: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

weekly.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
weekly.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

weekly.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
weekly.summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

weekly.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
weekly.summary: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

weekly.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
weekly.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

weekly.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
weekly.summary: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

weekly.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
weekly.summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

weekly.title: EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
weekly.summary: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.

weekly.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
weekly.summary: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

weekly.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
weekly.summary: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

weekly.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz
weekly.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a new bilateral treaty and hold talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France.

weekly.title: Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
weekly.summary: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

weekly.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
weekly.summary: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

weekly.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
weekly.summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

weekly.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
weekly.summary: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

weekly.title: As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
weekly.summary: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

weekly.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
weekly.summary: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.

weekly.title: Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
weekly.summary: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

weekly.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
weekly.summary: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

weekly.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
weekly.summary: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz rails against extremism, AfD sympathizers
weekly.summary: Political extremism threatens Germany's existing social order, Chancellor Merz has said. The Transport Ministry has proposed a five-year plan to improve Germany's ailing railroad infrastructure.

weekly.title: EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
weekly.summary: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

weekly.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
weekly.summary: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

weekly.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
weekly.summary: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."

weekly.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
weekly.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

weekly.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
weekly.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

weekly.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
weekly.summary: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

weekly.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
weekly.summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

weekly.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
weekly.summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

weekly.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party are all likely to dominate the campaign.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
